claims.text: Overall Green Flood in Afghanistan from 19 Jul 2026 01:00 UTC to 21 Jul 2026 01:00 UTC. Flood can have a low humanitarian impact based on the magnitude, exposed population and vulnerability. At least 20 people were killed, around 80 others injured, and more than 100 remain missing, in Nuristan Province following flash floods triggered by heavy rainfall.

UN News (22 July 2026): flash floods triggered by heavy rainfall on 20 July have killed at least 26 people across eastern Afghanistan, including 23 in Nuristan province, where homes, markets and roads were swept away, with the worst devastation in Parun City (7 houses completely destroyed, 23 partially damaged, 70 shops and 11 hotels damaged, 40 vehicles lost). The floods also killed three Afghan refugees at a returnee transit camp near the Torkham border crossing with Pakistan and injured nine others there. OCHA said the immediate priority is to save lives and reach people who may still be missing or injured, and warned that casualty figures could rise as more information becomes available; UNICEF and partners are setting up a field clinic in Parun for trauma care.

OCHA Flash Update #2: Flooding in Eastern Afghanistan (22-23 July 2026): in Parun City, Nuristan Province, local authorities report 23 killed, 5 missing (down from over 100) and 125 injured (38 severe, 87 minor). At the Torkham transit camp in Nangarhar, 3 Afghan refugees were killed and 9 injured (unchanged). One additional death is reported in Maidan Wardak province (Sayedabad District). The response has moved from immediate search and rescue and emergency life-saving assistance towards a broader, multi-sector response addressing shelter, health, food, WASH, protection, livelihoods and planning to address early recovery needs.

published.description: Torrential monsoon rains triggered flash floods in Afghanistan's eastern Nuristan province beginning around 19 July 2026, striking the provincial capital Parun and surrounding villages, and also killed Afghan refugees at a returnee transit camp near the Torkham border crossing. GDACS assessed the event as an overall Green alert for low humanitarian impact. OCHA's Flash Update #2 (23 July 2026) reports the confirmed death toll has held near 27 across eastern Afghanistan while the number of people missing in Nuristan has fallen sharply from over 100 to 5, and the response has now shifted from active search-and-rescue toward a broader multi-sector recovery effort covering shelter, health, food, WASH and protection needs.

impact.summary: OCHA's Flash Update #2 (23 July 2026) reports 23 people killed and 5 still missing (down from 100+) in Nuristan Province, with 125 injured (38 severe, 87 minor) there; the 3 Afghan refugees killed and 9 injured at the Torkham border transit camp are unchanged, and one additional death is reported in Maidan Wardak province (Sayedabad District) — a combined toll of 27 confirmed deaths across eastern Afghanistan. OCHA states the response has moved from immediate search-and-rescue toward a broader multi-sector recovery effort (shelter, health, food, WASH, protection, livelihoods); no authoritative source has declared the event resolved.

Algeria's interior ministry reported six deaths from the wildfires, and authorities reported more than 100 people hospitalised in the town of Seraidi and about 150 homes damaged there.

GDACS's event report for a second concurrent Green-alert forest fire in Algeria, now at episode 6 covering an 18-24 July 2026 window, cites about 14,082 hectares burned. Algeria's interior ministry registered six deaths in relation to the fires affecting multiple provinces during this period; four people were arrested on suspicion of deliberately starting fires.

GDACS's event report for a third concurrent Green-alert forest fire in Algeria, now at episode 5 covering a 21-24 July 2026 window, cites about 13,388 hectares burned, assessed as low humanitarian impact based on burned area and affected population. Thermal-anomaly detections continue to be recorded as of 24 July 2026.

Over the last 24 hours, the Ministry of the Interior, Local Authorities and Transport confirmed six fatalities linked to the wildfires. In Seraïdi, Annaba, more than 100 patients were evacuated from a rehabilitation hospital, while approximately 150 homes were affected or threatened. Preventive evacuations were also carried out in several localities, including El Tarf, Béjaïa, Guelma and Bouira.

published.description: A wave of wildfires swept northern Algeria's forested provinces (including Constantine and Seraïdi) from mid-to-late July 2026 amid a severe regional heatwave, with GDACS tracking three concurrent Green-alert fire complexes that together burned roughly 39,400 hectares. Algeria's interior ministry confirmed six deaths and authorities reported over 100 people hospitalised and about 150 homes damaged in the Seraïdi area, with preventive evacuations also carried out in El Tarf, Béjaïa, Guelma and Bouira; four people were arrested on suspicion of deliberately starting fires. As of 24-25 July 2026, GDACS records no further satellite thermal-anomaly detections for any of the three complexes, and Algerian civil protection authorities describe the blazes as under control.

impact.summary: GDACS's three concurrent Algeria wildfire complexes closed out at a combined ~39,400 hectares burned: the Seraïdi/Constantine complex (GDACS event 1029625, episode 8) at 11,864 ha with its final thermal-anomaly detection on 25 July; a second complex (event 1029611, episode 6) at 14,082 ha, last detection 24 July; and a third (event 1029618, episode 8) at 13,459 ha, last detection 24 July. With no new thermal detections since 24-25 July and civil protection authorities reporting the blazes under control, the event is assessed as contained.

claims.text: The Flash Update on flash floods and landslides in Chattogram Division has been prepared by the Needs Assessment and Information Management Working Group and published on 09 July 2026, reporting 7 districts affected, 536,000 people affected, 11 deaths, 17,000 people temporarily displaced and 1,700 shelters activated.

Flash Update #2 (dated 11 July 2026, published 13 July) reports that 10 districts have been affected, more than 1.07 million people have been impacted, over 36,000 people remain temporarily displaced, and 26 casualties have been reported.

Situation Report #1 (dated 13 July 2026, published 14 July) reports 51 reported fatalities and more than 1.11 million people affected across 10 districts (Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Bandarban, Khagrachhari, Rangamati, Moulvibazar, Sunamganj, Habiganj, Sylhet and Cumilla), with more than 38,000 people staying in over 1,000 evacuation shelters as of 12 July, and significant damage to homes, water systems, roads, bridges and public infrastructure.

Oxfam situation report on the Bangladesh flash floods (15 July 2026): 1.11 million people affected across 10 districts, 53 fatalities and 39 injuries reported as of 15 July; Chattogram district was hardest-hit, with Chattogram city recording 412.3mm of rain in 24 hours, the highest single-day July rainfall in 42 years.

BDRCS/IFRC nationwide situation report (14 July 2026): 1,074,534 people affected (NAWG figure) across 10 districts, about 38,500 people temporarily displaced (MoDMR figure) across 1,000+ shelters, 51 deaths, 267,918 households stranded, including 15 Rohingya refugee deaths reported by UNHCR among the Cox's Bazar camp toll.

BDRCS/IFRC nationwide situation report (posted 20 Jul 2026, originally published 19 Jul 2026): NAWG estimates 1,116,174 people affected across 10 districts (up from 1,074,534). MoDMR reports ~38,500 people temporarily displaced across 1,000+ shelters and 267,918 households stranded/isolated across seven districts (unchanged). At least 59 people have died nationwide (up from 53/51). In Cox's Bazar's 33 Rohingya refugee camps, flooding/landslides affected 28,000+ people, damaged 3,100+ shelters, and displaced 4,700+ individuals; UNHCR has confirmed 15 deaths among Rohingya refugees. As of 16 July only the Kushiyara River remained above danger level (at Markuli, Sunamganj and Fenchuganj, Sylhet), and water levels in the Surma (Sylhet/Sunamganj) and the Teesta, Dharla and Dudhkumar rivers (Rangpur Division) were falling.

Bangladesh Red Crescent Society Situation Report 4: Monsoon Flood & Landslide Response (posted 20 Jul 2026, originally published 17 Jul 2026), covering Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Bandarban, Rangamati, Khagrachhari, Cumilla, Moulvibazar, Habiganj, Sunamganj and Sylhet. As of 16 July 9:00 AM, only the Kushiyara River remained above danger level (Markuli/Sunamganj and Fenchuganj/Sylhet stations); the Someshwari River at Kalmakanda had receded below danger level; Surma river conditions in Sylhet/Sunamganj were expected to improve within 24 hours; Teesta, Dharla and Dudhkumar river levels in Rangpur Division were falling and projected to fall further. BDRCS Emergency Operations Centre remains active.

Oxfam/CODEC Rapid Needs Assessment (RNA) Report on the Bangladesh Flash Flood 2026 (posted 21 Jul 2026): deep-dive assessment of Satkania and Banshkhali upazilas (Chattogram Division) found 360,000+ people affected in Satkania and 110,000+ in Banshkhali; 90-95% of surveyed households reported partial/complete loss of belongings; 92% of drinking water sources damaged/contaminated (94% in Banshkhali lacking safe water); all assessed latrines submerged; 90% of households reported insufficient food access and 59% reported signs of malnutrition.

UN Resident Coordinator's Office Bangladesh Situation Report #2 (dated 23 July 2026, data as of 22 July) reports approximately 1.28 million people affected across seven of the hardest-hit districts, 59 deaths, 74,479 houses damaged or destroyed, and about 436,000 people assessed as requiring humanitarian assistance; food, cash, health, protection, shelter and WASH assistance activities remain active, with continued risk flagged from forecast heavy rainfall in affected districts.

claims.text: In the space of just three weeks, the UN Human Rights Office documented 15 drone strikes on El Obeid, which killed at least 45 civilians. El Obeid has more than half a million residents, together with at least 100,000 internally displaced persons, and the number of newly displaced people across Kordofan has risen by nearly two-thirds in only three months.

G7 Foreign Ministers' joint statement on El Obeid, Sudan (14 July 2026): condemns ongoing RSF drone strikes on El Obeid and obstruction of humanitarian access, references the precedent of atrocities in El Fasher, and calls for an immediate ceasefire and compliance with the Jeddah Declaration to protect civilians.

NRC report (posted 7 July 2026) on El Obeid: families are dying from drone strikes and from hunger as the siege continues, with an aid convoy struck the preceding week; essential services and food access are collapsing further as the blockade persists.

UN News (17 July 2026): the UN human rights chief warned that civilians in El Obeid "have been under siege for 18 months" and face continuous drone strikes, with more than 100,000 displaced people sheltering in camps in the city. WFP is providing food assistance to over 100,000 people in those camps, including nutrition support for 17,000 children, but is distributing only a reduced ration that recipients are sharing with other families. Almost 20 million people in Sudan are now classified as acutely food insecure, and more than 14 million people have been uprooted nationwide since the conflict began.

WFP Geneva Palais briefing note (published 17 July 2026): El Obeid city (population approximately 500,000) is hosting displaced people, with more than 120,000 people in the 'Unified IDP Camp' alone. WFP is providing food/cash assistance to just over 100,000 people in camps inside the city, but severe funding shortfalls mean recipients are only receiving 50 percent of the ration they should. Fuel scarcity has crippled partner logistics, forcing WFP to deploy its own fleet vehicles to keep distributions running.

UNFPA Flash Update #2 on the situation in El Obeid, North Kordofan, Sudan (published 20 July 2026, covering 1-19 July): 21 drone-related incidents were recorded in and around El Obeid between 1-19 July 2026, causing civilian casualties (no aggregate death toll given), damage to critical infrastructure, and further disruption to already-limited essential services, with severe constraints on sexual and reproductive health and gender-based-violence response services due to insecurity and resource shortages.

published.description: Rapid Support Forces (RSF) paramilitary forces have besieged El Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan state, subjecting the city of more than half a million residents to relentless drone strikes and blockade conditions. As of 20 July 2026, the siege continues with no ceasefire and no ground assault yet confirmed by authoritative sources, but drone strikes have intensified (21 incidents recorded 1-19 July per a UNFPA Flash Update on ReliefWeb, up from 15 strikes over three weeks in the prior UN Human Rights Office count) and the humanitarian situation has worsened: WFP reports more than 120,000 people are now sheltering in the city's Unified IDP Camp alone, with food rations cut to 50 percent of full entitlement due to funding shortfalls. No new aggregate civilian death toll has been issued since the UN's 3 July report of at least 45 killed. G7 foreign ministers condemned the siege on 14 July 2026, and UN officials continue to warn of the risk of large-scale atrocities similar to those already documented in El Fasher, Darfur.

impact.summary: No updated aggregate death toll has been published since the 3 July UN Human Rights Office figure (15 drone strikes over 3 weeks, at least 45 civilians killed); drone strikes have continued and even increased in frequency (21 drone-related incidents logged 1-19 July per a UNFPA Flash Update via ReliefWeb), but no authoritative source has issued a new cumulative casualty count as of 22 July 2026. On displacement, WFP (17 July briefing) confirms more than 120,000 people are now in the Unified IDP Camp alone in El Obeid, up from the previously reported '100,000+ displaced in city camps.' Rations for WFP-assisted families have been cut to 50 percent of the full entitlement due to funding shortfalls, a downgrade from the earlier 'reduced rations' description. No ceasefire, siege-lifting, or ground assault has been confirmed by an authoritative source.

claims.text: WHO/Europe's statement of 30 June 2026 reports that Spain's mortality monitoring system has already estimated more than 300 heat-associated excess deaths in just a few days, that emergency medical calls in France have risen by up to 50% in some cities, that London's ambulance service recorded its highest-ever number of life-threatening emergency calls in a single day, and that Italy reported 5 deaths in 24 hours during the heatwave.

WHO/Europe's statement of 7 July 2026, titled 'Extreme heat: more deadly weeks may still lie ahead for the European Region', warns that the current heatwave risk to health remains active and that heat-health action plans save lives.

WHO/Europe's statement of 16 July 2026, "Planning for a warmer world": "This summer's toll is still being counted but, already, data from just 5 countries shows nearly 10,000 excess deaths due to heat." WHO Regional Director Dr Hans Henri P. Kluge: "In the past 4 years alone, heat has claimed more than 200,000 lives, while heat-related mortality has risen by 30% over the past 20 years."

WHO/Europe issued successive public statements describing rising heat-associated mortality; its 16 July 2026 statement reported that data from just five countries already showed nearly 10,000 excess deaths from heat this summer, describing the season as a preview of a warmer future.

Its follow-up statement of 16 July 2026, "Planning for a warmer world," reported that data from just five countries already showed nearly 10,000 excess deaths due to heat this summer, and that heat has claimed more than 200,000 lives across the WHO European Region in the past four years, with heat-related mortality up 30% over the past two decades. claims.text: A magnitude 7.3 earthquake occurred on 17 July 2026 at 14:48:39 UTC, 58 km WSW of Puerto Madero, Mexico (14.6043N, 92.9517W), at a depth of approximately 18.6 km, in the subduction zone where the Cocos plate converges with North America at the Middle America Trench at approximately 76 mm/yr; the event occurred as reverse (thrust) faulting on or near the plate interface. Two small foreshocks preceded it, including a M4.1 on 14 July and a M4.7 88 minutes prior to the mainshock.

USGS's PAGER system assessed an alert level of Yellow for this earthquake, stating: "The USGS assesses that some damage and fatalities are possible, and that the impact should be relatively localized. Approximately four million people experienced Moderate (MMI V) to Very Strong (MMI VII) shaking." PAGER's probabilistic fatality model places roughly 66% probability on the event causing between 1 and 100 fatalities, and about 27% probability of exceeding 100 fatalities. No revision to this page has occurred since 18 July 2026.

claims.text: WHO Representative to Sudan Dr. Shible Sahbani reported more than 1,330 confirmed cholera cases and 114 confirmed deaths, a case fatality rate of 13.7 percent, in an outbreak affecting several states, mainly in the western part of the country, the Darfurs and the Kordofans, briefing journalists in Geneva on 10 July 2026. Aid officials say the true number of fatalities is likely much higher, and the disease is expected to spread further as the rainy season sets in, particularly among people who have fled towns and rural areas in North Kordofan.

UN News report (14 July 2026), citing OCHA, reconfirms WHO's count of 1,330 confirmed cholera cases and 114 deaths as of 7 July 2026, and describes the outbreak's continued spread: new confirmed and suspected cases in Kalma/Kampala displacement camp (South Darfur) and Tawila (North Darfur); West Kordofan reporting the highest caseload with new suspected cases and deaths; and North Kordofan reporting 32 new suspected cases in Gharb Bara locality in a single day. WHO delivered 8.5 tonnes of medical supplies to Kadugli and Dilling, South Kordofan — its first shipment there since December 2024 — and UNICEF delivered health supplies to El Fula, West Kordofan, serving about 429,000 people.

WFP report (data as of 17 July 2026): regular power outages are disrupting water supplies in El Obeid, and more than 30 new cholera cases have been recorded there as the city's displacement and hunger crisis deepens.

UN Women statement (24 July 2026): 'Cholera is already spreading in Sudan, with 1,330 cases reported by WHO in early July,' confirming no revised national cumulative total has superseded the 7 July WHO count as of this date.

published.description: Sudan's third cholera wave in as many years has spread across war-affected western and central states, principally Darfur and Kordofan, where conflict and constrained humanitarian access are hampering the response. WHO warns the outbreak could worsen further as the rainy season sets in and displacement continues around besieged cities such as El Obeid, where WFP reported more than 30 additional cases in mid-July. The national confirmed case/death count (1,330 cases, 114 deaths as of 7 July) remains WHO's latest published aggregate as of 24 July 2026, with continued geographic spread into new localities in North and West Kordofan and South Darfur.

impact.summary: WHO's Representative to Sudan reported (10 July 2026, Geneva briefing) more than 1,330 confirmed cholera cases and 114 confirmed deaths, a case fatality rate of 13.7%, in an outbreak affecting several western and central Sudanese states, mainly Darfur and Kordofan. That national aggregate remains WHO's latest published count as of 24 July 2026 — reconfirmed unchanged by a UN Women statement dated 24 July — but WFP reported in mid-July that more than 30 additional cholera cases had been recorded specifically in El Obeid, North Kordofan, as power outages disrupt water supplies there. OCHA reporting describes active geographic spread into Kalma/Kampala displacement camp (South Darfur), Tawila (North Darfur), West Kordofan and North Kordofan, as WHO and UNICEF scale up medical supply deliveries to Kadugli, Dilling and El Fula. Aid officials say the true toll is likely higher, and WHO warns the outbreak could worsen as the rainy season continues and conflict constrains the humanitarian response. No allowlisted source has declared the outbreak contained.

published.description: A tropical disturbance east-southeast of the Marianas organized into Tropical Depression 09W on 1 July 2026 and was named Bavi as a tropical storm on 2 July. Bavi underwent rapid intensification and reached Category 5 super typhoon strength by 4 July with sustained winds near 287 km/h, prompting GDACS to issue an overall Red alert as the storm tracked through Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands. After passing near Rota, the storm continued west, entering the Philippine Area of Responsibility on 8 July (locally named Inday), tracked across Taiwan and Japan's Ryukyu Islands, and made landfall in Zhejiang Province, eastern China, on 11 July before weakening over land.

GDACS's event report (current as of 12 July 2026) keeps the overall alert at Red for an event window of 01 Jul 2026 00:00 UTC to 11 Jul 2026 18:00 UTC, with a population of 35.3 million exposed to Category 1 (120 km/h) or higher winds; the current alert's urgency status is now 'Past', consistent with the storm weakening after landfall. claims.text: On 25 June 2026 a magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck 16 km SW of Moron in northern Venezuela, west of Caracas.

OCHA's Situation Report #22 (15 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report a toll of 4,829 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the 24 June earthquakes; 17,907 people remain without housing.

OCHA's Situation Report #23 (16 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report a toll of 4,930 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the 24 June earthquakes, with more than 1,308 aftershocks recorded and 17,907 people remaining without housing. The additional appeal was raised to US$299 million, still targeting 1.3 million people over six months. EU Commissioner for Crisis Management Hadja Lahbib conducted a field visit to La Guaira together with the UN Humanitarian Coordinator to review response efforts.

OCHA's Situation Report #24 (17 July 2026, 8:00 pm) states that, twenty-three days since the earthquakes, authorities report an official toll of 5,069 people dead and 16,740 injured, with 1,331 aftershocks recorded since the 24 June earthquakes (magnitude 7.2 and 7.5). An additional appeal for US$299 million remains in place to scale up the earthquake response for 1.3 million people over the next six months.

OCHA's Situation Report #26 (19 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report a toll of 5,208 people dead and 16,740 injured, with 1,388 aftershocks recorded since the 24 June earthquakes. An additional appeal for US$299 million remains in place to scale up the earthquake response for 1.3 million people over the next six months, on top of the US$632 million 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan.

Situation Report No. 28, Earthquakes in Venezuela, 21 July 2026, Time: 9:00 pm. Authorities report 1,405 aftershocks since the 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes that struck on 24 June. Official toll: 5,346 people dead and 16,740 injured. Authorities also indicated that 17,907 people lost their homes. The US$299 million addendum to the Humanitarian Response Plan complements the 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan, increasing the target population from 5.5 million to 6.2 million people and raising total funding requirements from US$632 million to US$931 million.

Situation Report No. 30, Earthquakes in Venezuela, 23 July 2026, Time: 09:00 pm. Authorities report 1,463 aftershocks since the 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes that struck on 24 June. Official toll: 5,398 people dead and 16,740 injured. Twenty-four days since the earthquakes, authorities report a toll of 5,398 people dead and 16,740 injured since the onset of the emergency. Authorities also indicated that 17,907 people lost their homes. Starting with this edition, the report will be published on a weekly basis. The next edition will be released on 30 July.
The USGS is assessing earthquake-triggered landslide hazards generated by the 2026 Venezuela earthquake sequence.

As of 1 July 2026, nearly 2,000 deaths have been confirmed and more than 6,400 people rescued; 1.8 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance including 680,000 children across six affected states, with around 1,000 buildings and over 400 schools damaged and more than 600 aftershocks recorded since the initial quakes.

OCHA's Situation Report #14 (07 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report an official toll of 3,685 people dead and 16,740 injured, with 6,462 people rescued since the 24 June earthquakes. Authorities also reported that approximately 17,907 people lost their homes and that more than 1,076 aftershocks have been recorded, with at least seven (7) states impacted and La Guaira remaining the most affected state.

OCHA's Situation Report #15 (08 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report an official toll of 3,811 people dead and 16,740 injured, with 6,462 people rescued since the 24 June earthquakes; approximately 17,907 people lost their homes and more than 1,100 aftershocks have been recorded. An additional appeal for US$296 million was launched to scale up the earthquake response for 1.3 million people over the next six months.

A first assessment by the UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) estimates direct physical damage to housing and infrastructure at some $37 billion, comprising $24 billion in damage to buildings and another $13 billion in infrastructure; at least 79 transitional camps have opened in stadiums and sports centres, hosting displaced residents and providing aid.

OCHA's Situation Report #18 (11 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that seventeen days after the earthquakes, authorities report a toll of 4,333 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the onset of the emergency; 1,171 aftershocks have been recorded, 17,907 people remain without housing, and 315 of those who died have yet to be identified. UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher concluded his four-day visit to the country and called for sustained international support for the Humanitarian Response Plan; an additional appeal for US$298 million was launched to address the multisectoral needs of 1.3 million people over the next six months.

OCHA's Situation Report No. 20 (13 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that, nineteen days since the earthquakes, authorities report a toll of 4,561 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the onset of the emergency, with more than 1,254 aftershocks recorded and 17,907 people remaining without housing. Authorities report at least 856 affected buildings, including 190 that have collapsed. The response continues with 107 transitional camps supporting affected populations, with a capacity of 25,064 people and a current occupancy of 20,231 people. A preliminary UNDP estimate indicates direct physical damage of US$6.7 billion, equivalent to 6 percent of GDP, alongside the earlier UNDRR estimate of approximately US$37 billion. The Government of Venezuela announced the creation of an initial reconstruction fund equivalent to US$200 million.

OCHA's Situation Report #21 (14 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report a toll of 4,734 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the 24 June earthquakes; 17,907 people remain without housing.

published.description: A magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck northern Venezuela west of Caracas on 25 June 2026, 39 seconds after a magnitude 7.2 foreshock in the same sequence. The USGS assessed that high casualties and widespread damage are probable, and the national government of Venezuela declared a state of emergency. A month on, the confirmed death toll has continued to climb past 5,390, and the UN humanitarian response has scaled up further, with combined funding requirements now exceeding $900 million.

impact.summary: As of OCHA Situation Report #30 (23 July 2026, 9:00 pm), 29 days after the 24 June doublet quakes, the official toll stands at 5,398 dead and 16,740 injured (up from 5,346 dead in SitRep #28 two days earlier), with 1,463 aftershocks recorded (up from 1,405) and 17,907 people who lost their homes. Funding and targeting figures are unchanged: the combined 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan plus the US$299 million addendum still totals US$931 million in requirements, targeting 6.2 million people, of whom 1.3 million are earthquake-affected. OCHA has shifted from near-daily to weekly situation reports starting with #30, with the next edition due 30 July 2026 — a de-escalation signal, though not a declaration that the response has concluded. Earlier assessments put direct physical damage at $37 billion (UNDRR) and $6.7 billion / 6% of GDP (UNDP).
